body:
## Summary

Add a Qwen3-TTS 0.6B CustomVoice streaming Node to the existing Graph Editor, backed by an extension-owned local Worker and pinned, reviewed browser assets. Deliver incremental PCM through an explicit producer-independent typed port to Speaker.

**Draft / partial implementation of #168:** Qwen3-TTS has real local MV3 streaming evidence. CosyVoice3 remains unsupported and is absent from the palette/runtime: the reviewed browser export finalizes whole utterances and needs further export/runtime work. The CosyVoice3 scope decision has not been approved or split out. Do not merge as full resolution of #168 until that scope is resolved.

## Outcome

- English and Japanese PCM begins rendering before synthesis completes. Committed text is processed as ordered utterances; provisional text is rejected.
- Speaker validates stream identity, sequence and boundaries, schedules chunks continuously, converts sample rates, and bounds accepted audio. Stop drains accepted work; Cancel halts generation/playback and suppresses late replies.
- Save/Models explicitly prepares hash-pinned assets; Start uses cached assets only. Existing MV3 CSP, model diagnostics and activation from the Start gesture are retained.
- Existing Supertonic3, Kokoro, completed-clip Speaker and manual Audio player/WAV behavior remain intact. Saved graphs need no new migration.
- Separate candidate conclusions, tokenizer/vocoder/runtime pins, licenses and resource limitations are recorded in [streaming TTS documentation](docs/streaming-tts.md).

## Validation

Implementation-stage results and raw timing/audio artifacts: [docs/evidence/streaming-tts-168.md](docs/evidence/streaming-tts-168.md).

- 736 unit tests passed, including stream boundaries, ordering/replay, queue bounds, Stop/Cancel, late replies, graph persistence, preparation and cache failures.
- 2 real-model packaged MV3 tests passed with pinned assets: decoder continuity and saved-graph English/Japanese playback, consecutive utterances, Stop/Cancel and offline cache-only Start. First nonzero render versus synthesis EOS: English 1,966.45 vs 5,316.54 ms; Japanese 619.21 vs 5,324.40 ms.
- 3 existing completed-clip Speaker browser tests passed.
- Full extension preparation/build passed; model files and packaged sources were verified against their pinned hashes/worktree.
- Publication checks: worktree clean, current main is an ancestor, and `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` passed. Implementation tests were not rerun during publication.

Real-model evidence is from one Apple M4 Max / 64 GiB machine running Chrome 156 with Metal WebGPU and a 48 kHz AudioContext. Browser rendering was measured; physical loudspeaker acoustics were not. Other hardware, minimum/peak memory, long sessions and GPU-loss recovery remain unqualified. No CosyVoice3 browser inference or pre-EOS playback is claimed.

**Required post-merge verification remains pending:** repeat the packaged-extension checks from the merged commit using exact pins, record first-chunk/render/EOS timestamps and hardware/peak memory, and verify consecutive utterances, Stop/Cancel and offline Start. This PR is not a claim of production verification.

## Related issues

Closes #168

This PR remains draft. Resolve the outstanding CosyVoice3 scope decision before merge; required post-merge verification remains pending. The closing reference is included as explicitly required by this publication task and does not establish that the remaining acceptance criteria are complete.

## Scope check

- [ ] This PR fully addresses each Issue it claims to resolve.
- [x] This PR does not include unrelated work.
- [x] This PR does not add speculative abstractions, extensibility, frameworks, or subsystems that are not needed by the Issue.
- [ ] Any intentionally partial implementation is clearly stated, and the parent Issue is not presented as fully resolved unless the remaining scope has been explicitly split out.
- [x] Validation maps to the Issue's expected outcome / acceptance criteria.
